narrative: On 28 February 2017 an Amazon S3 operator executed a playbook command with a mistyped parameter, removing far more capacity than intended and forcing a full restart of the index and placement subsystems in US-EAST-1 for approximately four hours.
root_cause: The operational tool accepted an unbounded server-count parameter, so a single typo crossed two independent minimum-redundancy thresholds simultaneously. The two affected subsystems had not been cold-restarted for years and took hours to rebuild state.
impact_bullets: Roughly 4 hours of S3 unavailability in US-EAST-1
Dependent AWS services and thousands of customer workloads affected
Index and placement subsystems required full state rebuild
lesson_domain_bullets: Operational tools need parameter bounds, not just authentication
Cold-start time must be a known quantity, not an unknown
